g1.correct: I didn't see nobody at the party.
accept: I didn't see nobody at the party.
g1.label: 1. Which has a double negative?
g1.why: Two negatives in one clause: standard English uses 'didn't see anybody'.

g2.correct: The sun shining brightly, we decided to go for a walk.
accept: The sun shining brightly, we decided to go for a walk.
g2.label: 2. Which contains an absolute phrase?
g2.why: An absolute phrase has its own subject plus a participle and modifies the whole sentence.

g3.correct: The cake was baked by my mother.
accept: The cake was baked by my mother.
g3.label: 3. Simple passive with a past participle?
g3.why: Simple past passive is was/were + past participle, for one completed action.

g4.correct: She stopped to rest for a while.
accept: She stopped to rest for a while.
g4.label: 4. Which has a non-finite clause?
g4.why: A non-finite clause has no tensed verb; 'to rest' is an infinitive of purpose.

g5.correct: My brother, a talented artist, lives in Berlin.
accept: My brother, a talented artist, lives in Berlin.
g5.label: 5. Which contains an appositive?
g5.why: The comma-marked noun phrase renames 'my brother' without adding a verb.

g6.correct: I like to play, when I have free time, video games.
accept: I like to play, when I have free time, video games.
g6.label: 6. Which is a split construction?
g6.why: A clause is wedged between the verb and its object, splitting 'play' from 'video games'.

g7.correct: I had been studying for hours when I finally took a break.
accept: I had been studying for hours when I finally took a break.
g7.label: 7. Which is past perfect continuous?
g7.why: Past perfect continuous is 'had been' + -ing, for a longer action before a past point.

g8.label: 8. Which word is a preposition?
g8.why: Prepositions show position or direction before a noun: under the table.

g9.correct: To get to the park, my bicycle was the fastest option.
accept: To get to the park, my bicycle was the fastest option.
g9.label: 9. Which has a dangling infinitive?
g9.why: The infinitive needs a person to perform it, and a bicycle cannot get to the park.

g10.correct: I look forward to the weekend.
accept: I look forward to the weekend.
g10.label: 10. Phrasal-prepositional verb?
g10.why: A phrasal-prepositional verb is verb + adverb + preposition: look + forward + to.
